exposure: Allergy Clarification for Cefazolin Evidence-based Prescribing Tool (ACCEPT)
cohort: The study included 3128 eligible women who underwent a cesarean delivery, 282 (9%) of whom reported a beta-lactam allergy.
finding: Implementation of a simple allergy history-guided algorithm resulted in a statistically significant and sustained increase in perioperative cefazolin prophylaxis among obstetrical patients with reported beta-lactam allergy.
mod_finding: Implementation of the algorithm in patients undergoing cesarean delivery led to a sustained increase in perioperative cefazolin prophylaxis from 52% to 87% (and remaining high at 92% after 2 years).
